gaps.title: Mandatory rejection reason not supported by the captured Reject action
gaps.description: DEC-003 confirms that a reason is required when a manager rejects a request and that the employee sees it. The captured detail screen shows only Approve and Reject buttons with no field for a reason, and the state after pressing Reject is not shown in the capture. Where the reason is entered, what happens if it is left empty, and where the employee later sees it are unspecified.
gaps.why_it_matters: Rejecting without a reason would break a confirmed customer rule, and the employee needs the reason to correct and resubmit the request (DEC-003).
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A rejection could be recorded with no reason, leaving the employee unable to understand or correct the request.

gaps.title: Approver eligibility and the 'manager away' substitute rule
gaps.description: DEC-002 confirms that only a request's direct manager may approve or reject it, and that the manager's own manager may act when the manager is away. The capture shows Approve and Reject as enabled on the detail screen with no indication of who sees them. How 'away' is determined, whether the direct manager can still act when a substitute has acted, what non-eligible users see on the detail screen, and how a manager's own leave request is handled are not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[element_ref=SCR-005] 'Who can approve or reject a request'

gaps.why_it_matters: Approval is the core control of this feature; the substitute rule introduces a second eligible approver whose eligibility depends on an undefined 'away' condition.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests could be approved by ineligible people, or block indefinitely when the direct manager is absent and the substitute cannot act.
research_questions: How do established HR leave systems model a temporary approver when the line manager is absent (out-of-office flag, delegation period, escalation after a time limit)?

gaps.title: Content and validation of a new leave request are unknown
gaps.description: The New request page failed to capture (HTTP 404), so its fields are not shown in the capture. CQ-001 (what an employee provides when submitting) was recorded against DEC-001, but DEC-001's verbatim text is about rejection reasons and resubmission and does not answer it. DEC-004 says employees see each request's dates, while the captured list shows only leave type and a duration in days. Required fields, date rules (past dates, overlaps with existing requests, half days) and error behaviour are unspecified.
gaps.why_it_matters: Submitting a request is the entry point of the whole feature (REQ-001), and the data entered determines what managers decide on and what employees later see.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The request data model, the submission form and its validation cannot be specified.
research_questions: Which validation rules do common leave-management products apply to leave request dates (overlapping requests, past dates, partial days, public holidays)?

gaps.title: Rejected and Cancelled statuses: who can cancel and when
gaps.description: DEC-004 confirms four statuses: pending, approved, rejected and cancelled. Only Pending and Approved appear in the capture. Who may cancel a request (employee, manager), in which statuses cancellation is allowed (pending only, or also approved leave), and how Rejected and Cancelled requests appear are not stated and not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: The confirmed status set includes a Cancelled state with no defined trigger or actor, so the request lifecycle cannot be completed.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Cancellation could be permitted to the wrong person or in the wrong state, for example cancelling leave already taken.

gaps.title: Correct-and-resubmit flow for rejected requests
gaps.description: DEC-003 confirms that a rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted. No screen or action for this appears in the capture. Whether resubmission reopens the same request or creates a new one, what happens to the earlier rejection reason, whether there is a limit on resubmissions, and who reviews it are unspecified. Whether a pending (not rejected) request can be edited was asked in CQ-003 and not answered.
gaps.why_it_matters: Resubmission changes the lifecycle (a rejected request is not terminal) and affects which status and history the employee and manager see.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The status model and request history cannot be specified, and rejection reasons may be lost on resubmission.

gaps.title: Detail view content for non-pending requests is unobserved
gaps.description: DEC-004 confirms that employees see each request's status, dates and the manager's comment. The only captured detail screen shows a pending request with status and Approve/Reject buttons; dates and a manager's comment are not shown in the capture. The detail page for the approved Sick leave request failed to capture (HTTP 404), so what a decided request shows and whether it offers any actions is unknown.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[element_ref=SCR-003] 'What does the Sick leave detail screen show'

gaps.why_it_matters: Seeing status, dates and the manager's comment is the confirmed content of REQ-003, and the screen that would show a decided request was not captured.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The employee-facing status view cannot be specified for approved, rejected or cancelled requests.

gaps.title: Status-change emails: recipients, content and delivery failure
gaps.description: DEC-004 confirms that employees are emailed whenever a request's status changes. Whether managers (or the substitute manager) are emailed when a request is submitted or resubmitted, what each email contains, whether the rejection reason or sick-leave details are included, and what happens when an email fails to deliver are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Email is the confirmed way employees learn of decisions; without a manager-side trigger, pending requests may go unnoticed, especially when the substitute rule applies.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Employees may miss decisions silently on delivery failure, and managers may never learn a request awaits them.
research_questions: What practices do transactional email services recommend for detecting and handling bounced or failed notification emails?

gaps.title: Which requests appear in the list for employees versus managers
gaps.description: The captured list shows two requests with no indication of whose they are. Whether an employee sees only their own requests, whether a manager sees their direct reports' requests in the same list or elsewhere, and what a substitute manager sees are not stated and not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[element_ref=SCR-003] 'Which requests does a user see'

gaps.why_it_matters: Leave records include sick leave and manager comments; showing them to the wrong person exposes personal data, while hiding them from the right manager blocks approval.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Data visibility rules for the list cannot be specified, and managers may have no route to the requests they must decide.

gaps.title: Reversibility and confirmation of approve and reject decisions
gaps.description: CQ-002 asked whether a decision can be reversed; DEC-002 does not answer that part. The capture shows Approve and Reject as single buttons; no confirmation step or post-decision state is shown in the capture. Whether an approved request can later be changed or revoked by a manager, and whether a mistaken click can be undone, are unspecified.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[element_ref=SCR-005] 'Is a decision reversible once made?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Each decision triggers an email to the employee (DEC-004), so a mistaken approval or rejection is communicated immediately and may be acted on.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Mistaken decisions cannot be corrected under defined rules, or are corrected ad hoc without the employee being informed consistently.

gaps.title: Two eligible approvers acting on the same request
gaps.description: Under DEC-002 both the direct manager and, when the manager is away, the manager's own manager can act, and one approval is enough. What happens when both act on the same request at nearly the same time, or when one acts on a stale view after the other has already decided, is not stated. Repeated clicks on Approve or Reject are also unaddressed.
gaps.why_it_matters: The confirmed substitute rule creates two people able to decide the same request, so conflicting outcomes (one approves, one rejects) are possible.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A request could end in an inconsistent state or the employee could receive contradictory emails.
research_questions: What patterns do approval workflow systems use to prevent two approvers recording conflicting decisions on the same item (optimistic concurrency checks, state-transition guards)?

gaps.title: Empty, loading, success and error states for the list and decisions
gaps.description: The capture shows only a default list with two items and a pending detail screen. What the list shows when a user has no requests, while loading, and what confirmation or error follows Approve, Reject or submission are not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[element_ref=SCR-005] 'What confirmation, error or failure state follows'
ambiguous_behaviours[element_ref=SCR-003] 'what is shown when it is empty'

gaps.why_it_matters: A new employee's first view is an empty list, and managers need to know whether a decision was recorded before the employee is emailed.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users cannot tell whether submissions and decisions succeeded, leading to repeat actions or missed failures.
research_questions: What do established design systems (for example GOV.UK Design System) recommend for confirmation and error messages after submitting or approving a request?

gaps.title: Traceability of who decided a request
gaps.description: With a substitute approver allowed (DEC-002) and resubmission allowed (DEC-003), whether the system must record who approved, rejected or cancelled each request, when, and with what reason is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: When the deciding manager may not be the direct manager, the employee and HR need to know who actually made the decision.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Disputed leave decisions cannot be traced to a person or time.
research_questions: What audit information do UK employment record-keeping practices expect for leave approval decisions, and for how long?

gaps.title: Sick leave as health data: visibility, comments and retention
gaps.description: The capture lists Sick leave as a leave type alongside annual leave. Who may see sick-leave requests and any reasons or comments attached, whether these appear in status-change emails, and how long such records are kept are not stated.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-011 field 'Leave type (Annual leave, Sick leave)'

gaps.why_it_matters: Sick-leave records can reveal health information about employees, and this feature shows them in lists, detail screens and emails.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Health-related personal data may be over-shared or kept longer than permitted.
research_questions: How does UK GDPR treat sick-leave records and reasons as special category (health) data, and what does the ICO's employment practices guidance say about who may access them and retention?

gaps.title: Accessibility of status text and decision feedback
gaps.description: Status is shown as text in the list and on the detail screen, and the outcome after Approve or Reject is not shown in the capture. How status changes and decision outcomes are conveyed to assistive technology users is unspecified.
gaps.why_it_matters: Employees and managers rely on status and decision feedback to complete this workflow; the Open links in the list also share a visible label.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Screen-reader users may not learn whether a decision was recorded or which request a given Open link refers to.
research_questions: What do WCAG 2.2 success criteria 4.1.3 (Status Messages) and 2.4.4 (Link Purpose) require for repeated 'Open' links and post-action status feedback?

gaps.title: Effect of decisions on leave balances
gaps.description: Whether approving, cancelling or resubmitting a request changes an employee's leave balance, and whether balances are shown anywhere in this feature, is not stated in the requirements or decisions and is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Annual leave is a limited entitlement; if balances are in scope, approval and cancellation must keep them consistent.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Scope of the feature is unclear and balances could drift from approved leave if handled elsewhere.

assumptions.text: CQ-001 is treated as unanswered because DEC-001's verbatim text addresses rejection reasons and resubmission, not the content of a leave request.
assumptions.why: DEC-001 was matched to CQ-001 by keywords and its wording does not answer the question asked.
assumptions.impact: GAP-003 is raised as critical and REQ-001 is proposed as unknown.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm with the customer what information an employee provides when submitting a leave request.

assumptions.text: The captured list screen is treated as a single view whose audience (employee, manager or both) is unknown.
assumptions.why: The capture gives no indication of the signed-in user or whose requests are listed.
assumptions.impact: Visibility and approver-eligibility gaps (GAP-002, GAP-008) are raised rather than inferred from the mockup.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm which users see the list and whether managers have a separate view of their reports' requests.

proposed_status_changes.reason: The information a leave request contains is not stated; CQ-001 was recorded against DEC-001, whose answer does not address it, and the New request page was not captured.
